source_title: Mark a claim and an example
source_description: Mark which sentence states the claim and which sentence is only an example.
Name the person whose words appear as a quote and the person who wrote the surrounding text.

source_title: Separate an ad from the report
source_description: Point to the part of a page that is selling something and the part that is reporting.

source_title: Write a claim you can check
source_description: Write one sentence another person can check, and name where they would look.
Find one number that differs between two versions of the same note.

source_title: Name the audience of a poster
source_description: Say who a poster is speaking to, using the words and the place it hangs.

source_title: Tell a preview from a review
source_description: Say whether a short text is selling a future showing or responding to a work the writer saw.
On one page, say which date is the event and which date is the publication.
Mark one word that judges and one word that only describes.
Name one fact, person, or group a short piece does not mention, and why that matters to the claim.

source_title: Test a caption against the picture
source_description: Say one thing a caption claims that the picture shows, and one thing it does not show.

source_title: Save a clip with its page
source_description: Save a short clip or quote only together with the page or person it came from.

source_title: Turn a headline into a question
source_description: Turn a headline into a question the article might answer, then see whether it does.

source_title: Say when a number is rounded
source_description: Say whether a printed number is a count you could check or a round figure.
Draw a box around the part of a page that asks for money, a click, or a signup.

source_title: Write what would change your mind
source_description: Write one observation that would make you drop a claim you currently hold.

source_title: Take an offer and add a fact
source_description: In a made-up scene, accept what the other person just said and add one new fact.
Tell a small real event again from the place of another person who was there.
Tell a short story and stop when it turns, then ask what the listener expects.

source_title: Describe a room by three sounds
source_description: Describe a room using three sounds, without naming an object you cannot hear.
Change one rule of a game you already know, play one short round, and say what the change did.
Invent a character with one want and one obstacle, then play that for one minute.
Order six quick sketches so another person can say what happened.
Cut a short story until one turn remains, and read that version aloud.
Stop your sentence and let the other person say the next line of a made-up scene.

source_title: Set a scene with three objects
source_description: Place three objects and say what happened in the moment just before.
Repeat one invented fact in the same words when someone asks again later in the scene.
End a one-minute story on an image, not on a moral.
Answer three questions in a character's voice without adding a new power.
Tell two events in the other order and say what the listener now believes.

source_title: Leave a prop for the next person
source_description: Leave one object and a one-line note so the next person can continue a scene.
Start a one-minute story from a sound you just heard, and name the sound.

source_title: Keep one reveal for the end
source_description: Hold one fact until the last line, and say why the story needed it there.

source_title: Read a year on a building
source_description: Read a year cut or fixed on a building and write one thing that year does not tell you.

source_title: Find one change in an old photo
source_description: Name one thing present in both an old photo and the place now, and one thing gone.

source_title: Copy an inscription and mark a doubt
source_description: Copy a short inscription and mark any letter you are not sure of.

source_title: Say who a memorial speaks to
source_description: Read a short memorial and say who it addresses.
Put three objects in order of wear and name the clue you used.

source_title: Mark a guess about a place name
source_description: Read a street or room name and write what it might refer to, marked as a guess.
Name one visible clue that places an old photo in time, and the limit of that clue.

source_title: Separate a memory from a paper
source_description: Write one thing a person remembers and one thing a paper shows about the same event.
Find a maker's mark on a tool or dish and copy only what you can see.

source_title: Ask what a plaque does not say
source_description: Read a plaque and write one question it does not answer.
Find one word that differs between two editions or printings of the same short text.

source_title: Place a song with a named clue
source_description: Name one musical or lyric clue and the period it suggests, marked as a guess.
Copy a historical name as printed, including a spelling you would not use now.

source_title: Read a name on a bench
source_description: Read a dedication on a bench or similar gift and say what it does not tell you about the place.

source_title: Note a repair on an old object
source_description: Point to a repair on an old object and say what the repair tells you and what it does not.

source_title: Change one fold on a paper plane
source_description: Change one fold on a paper plane and say whether that flight went farther.

source_title: Watch water appear on a glass
source_description: Watch a cold glass and say where water appeared on the outside.
Mark the edge of a puddle and note later the same day whether it is smaller.
Roll two different shapes down the same slope and say which went farther.
Balance a ruler and move a small weight until it tips, then say where the weight was.
Leave a small salt solution and describe what you see the next day, without claiming a yield.
Clap once in two places and say where you heard the clap come back.
Bend drinking straws into two shapes and say which held a light book longer.
Overlap two pieces of colored transparent film and name the color you see.
Make two paper spinners, change one thing, and say which spun longer.
Span a gap with paper and add one fold so a light object can sit on it.

source_title: Roll a ball on two floors
source_description: Roll the same ball on two surfaces and say which one slowed it sooner.
Tap two lids and say which one rings longer.
Stretch a rubber band and say how the sound changed when you plucked it.

source_title: Weigh two shapes of the same clay
source_description: Shape the same piece of clay two ways and say whether the scale number stayed the same.

source_title: Drop a sheet and a crumple
source_description: Drop a flat sheet and a crumpled sheet of the same paper and say which landed first.

source_title: Slide a block on two surfaces
source_description: Slide the same small block on two surfaces and say which one stopped sooner.

source_title: See which way a spinner turns
source_description: Launch a simple spinner twice, once with each hand direction, and say which way it turned.
Write the start, one middle point, and the end time for a small gathering.
Name who will do a job and who will do it if that person is late.
Count the chairs and say whether a named list of people can sit.

source_title: Write where you go if it rains
source_description: Write in one sentence where the group goes if it rains, and how they will know.
Put one labeled spot for lost items and tell the group where it is.
Write who has the key or the responsibility to leave the room as agreed.
Collect one sentence from each person on a card and read the cards without ranking the people.

source_title: Write what a late person needs
source_description: Write the one sentence a person who arrives late needs in order to join.
Put the end time where a person who just arrived can read it.
Say what may be photographed before people arrive, and where that rule is written.
Write a name large enough to read from the other side of a table.
Pair people who have not already been talking, and give them one question.
List items the group borrowed and tick each one when it is back.
Write the order of three speakers and the sentence that hands the turn on.

source_title: Match the room to the start
source_description: Take a photo at the start and leave the room matching it, or list what you changed on purpose.

source_title: Put the agenda at the entrance
source_description: Place the agenda where a person entering can see it without asking.

source_title: Leave a path to the door
source_description: Leave a clear path from the seats to the door, and show it to one person.
Draw one arrow that touches the part you mean, and ask someone to name that part.
Take two photos of one object, one higher and one lower, and say what each shows.
Show two images in the same frame and label the one thing that changed.

source_title: Make the heading the only large type
source_description: Make one heading visibly larger than the body, and leave the body one size.

source_title: Ask someone to name your mark
source_description: Draw a simple mark and write the word another person uses for it.

source_title: Keep the label in the crop
source_description: Crop a photo and keep a label readable in the frame.

source_title: Use one color for the change
source_description: Use one color only for the thing that changed, and leave the rest in one other treatment.

source_title: Draw the hand on the step
source_description: Draw a hand on an object to show one step of a task.
Place a title and ask someone where they looked first.

source_title: Put a known object for scale
source_description: Put a known object in the frame and say what size it gives the subject.
Number three steps on one drawing in the order they are done.

source_title: Remove a mark that does not explain
source_description: Remove one decorative mark from a diagram and say what became clearer.
Write a caption that says what changed, not how you feel about it.

source_title: Record their word for a symbol
source_description: Show a symbol and write the word the other person used, even if it is not yours.

source_title: Show every step of one example
source_description: Write one worked example with every step visible, including the last result.

source_title: Mark which answer used the notes
source_description: Write three questions, answer them, and mark which answer used the notes.

source_title: Show the line that fixes a step
source_description: Show one wrong step and the line that fixes it.

source_title: Watch them do the next step
source_description: Stop an explanation and let the learner do the next step while you watch.
When a learner asks the same question again, stop and write that question down.
Write the one thing you will practice next, and where you will do it.

source_title: Pick the explanation you can use
source_description: Read two short explanations and say which one you can follow without the author present.

source_title: Log a mistake and its cue
source_description: Write three mistakes you made on a task and the cue that would have stopped each one.

source_title: Teach with the object in their hands
source_description: Teach one step while the object is in the learner's hands, not yours.
Ask what the learner thinks will happen, then show the result.
Write a hint that says where to look, not the answer.

source_title: Try the step on a new case
source_description: Give a new example and see whether the learner uses the same step.
Cover a worked answer, try the step, then uncover and compare.

source_title: Write the step in their words
source_description: Ask the learner to say the step, and write it in their words.
After you agree a time, write it back and ask the other person to correct it.
Offer two times or two choices, then stop talking.
When someone declines, repeat the no and do not add a new offer in the same breath.
Say the idea you disagree with and one reason, without a remark about the person.

source_title: Ask what they want from you
source_description: Ask whether they want a listener, a suggestion, or help, before you offer a fix.

source_title: Write the owner of the decision
source_description: Write the decision and the one person who will carry it.
Stop and name the person who has the next turn.

source_title: Write what you will not do
source_description: Write what you will not do, in one sentence the other person can repeat.
Stop your sentence when someone else starts, and let them finish.
Read the decision back in their words before you leave.

source_title: Ask a closed question, then an open one
source_description: Ask one yes-or-no question, then one question that needs a sentence.
Say the assumption the plan depends on, and ask if it is still true.

source_title: Write when you will check again
source_description: Write when you will look at a task again, and what will count as done.
Say whose point changed a decision, in front of the people who were there.
When a task stalls, offer one smaller step the other person can accept or refuse.

source_title: Separate the fact you both see
source_description: Write one fact you can both point to, separate from what each of you prefers.

source_title: Rinse a brush until the water runs clear
source_description: Rinse a paintbrush and stop when the water runs clear.

source_title: Mend a tear from the back
source_description: Mend a torn page from the back so the text on the front stays readable.

source_title: Ease an edge until cloth passes
source_description: Smooth one rough edge until a cloth passes over it without catching.

source_title: Oil a dry spoon and wipe it
source_description: Rub food-safe oil on a dry wooden spoon and wipe off the excess.

source_title: Press one leaf and date it
source_description: Press one fallen leaf flat and write the date you will look at it again.
Bind the end of a cord so it does not fray, then tug the binding.
Sew a short hem on scrap cloth with stitches you can point to.
Choose a thread closer in color to a cloth than another thread, and say why.

source_title: Rest a brush so the bristles stay straight
source_description: Put a damp brush where the bristles are not bent, and look at it the next day.

source_title: Hang a bundle where air reaches
source_description: Tie a small bundle of herbs or flowers so air can reach it, and hang it where you said.

source_title: Wax a thread and sew an inch
source_description: Wax a short thread and sew one inch so the thread does not tangle.
Patch a small paper hole from behind and write on the front.

source_title: Coil a hose with the end on top
source_description: Coil a hose or cable so the end you need is on top and it does not kink.

source_title: Note the light on a color sample
source_description: Label a color sample with the light you viewed it in.

source_title: Check a strip at both ends
source_description: Cut one strip along a guide and measure the width at both ends.

source_title: Stitch a pamphlet so it opens
source_description: Stitch a few sheets into a pamphlet that opens and stays together.

source_title: Follow a brush label or stop
source_description: Clean a brush only in the way its label describes, or stop if there is no label.

source_title: File a snag until cloth passes
source_description: File one snag on a piece of wood until a cloth passes over it.

source_title: Sort screws by the head you can see
source_description: Sort a small mix of screws by the head you can see, into labeled cups.
Test a glue on a scrap of the same material before you use it on the real piece.

source_title: Sketch posture without naming a species
source_description: Sketch a bird or animal's posture and write that you are not naming the species.

source_title: Count calls and write the place
source_description: Count calls for a short, stated time and write the place and the hour.

source_title: Note which way a tree leans
source_description: Note which way a tree leans and what stands beside it.
Say which of two marks looks sharper, and what you will not conclude about what made them.
Note which blooms on one plant are open and which are closed at two times of day.

source_title: Show the place matches the start
source_description: List or photograph a spot before you use it, then show it matches when you leave.
Show that what you carried out of a place matches what you brought in, plus any litter you meant to remove.

source_title: Draw one landmark on the skyline
source_description: Draw a skyline and mark one landmark you could find again.

source_title: Name the wind by a landmark
source_description: Write where the wind came from by pointing to a landmark, not a guessed degree.

source_title: Measure one plant and date it
source_description: Measure one plant against a ruler and write the date.

source_title: Mark three sounds on a line
source_description: Draw a short walk as a line and mark three sounds where you heard them.
Name one thing you could take and then leave it where it is.

source_title: Note two sides of a path
source_description: Write one difference between the two sides of a path.
Watch a cloud shadow cross the ground and say which way it went.
Photograph or list a setting before you change it, then show what you moved.
Save a copy under a new name and show that the original file or page did not change.

source_title: Write the version on the page
source_description: Write a version mark on a page and say what changed from the previous one.
Move a draft you are finished with into a place you named, and leave a working file separate.
Open the file you sent and match one sentence to the draft you meant to send.

source_title: Write what you did not change
source_description: Write three lines: what changed, why, and what you left alone.
Mark one page as finished and make the next change only on a new page.

source_title: Pick the latest name, then open it
source_description: Choose the latest of three files from the date in the name, then open it to check.

source_title: Save a link under your title
source_description: Save a link with a title you wrote, not only the title the page gave you.
Write the visible sign of done before you start a small task.
Undo the last change on a practice page or file and show the previous state.
Name the piece you are missing and the place you already looked.
Write the one limit on a task, then do the task inside it.

source_title: Stop when the question is answered
source_description: Stop a piece of work when the result answers the question you wrote down.
List two things that will stay the same, then change one other thing.

source_title: Write the question before you search
source_description: Write the question on paper before you open a search.
Make the cut on a scrap before you cut the piece you mean to keep.

source_title: Mark a line tools will not cross
source_description: Mark a line on the table and keep tools on the work side of it.

source_title: Sit where they can see you
source_description: Sit where the person you are with can see your face without turning sharply.

source_title: Ask before you move their object
source_description: Ask before you move an object that belongs to the person you are helping.

source_title: Leave a note in their words
source_description: Leave a short note using words the person chose for what they need.
Agree a signal that means pause, and use it once.
Invite a person who has not spoken, once, and accept it if they do not take the turn.

source_title: Stop a joke that leaves someone out
source_description: Stop a joke you were telling when you see it leaves someone out.

source_title: Close a gap in the circle
source_description: Move your own chair so a person can join the circle without climbing over anyone.

source_title: Write a question for the meeting
source_description: Write one question you could ask at a public meeting, and what answer would help.
Read a closing date on a notice and say what closes on that date.

source_title: Find where a form goes back
source_description: Find where a form should be returned, from the form itself.
Compare the hours of two nearby services and say which one is open at a time you name.

source_title: Read a rule on a door
source_description: Read a rule posted on a door and say what you will do because of it.
Read a ratio such as one to four and say what one part means in the thing you are looking at.
Walk a distance you estimated in paces, then check it against a known measure.
Read how much time is left until a moment you can see on a clock.

source_title: Pin a hem before you sew
source_description: Pin a hem on scrap cloth, check the length, then sew or unpin.

source_title: Fold a scarf so the ends meet
source_description: Fold or hang a scarf so the ends meet where you intended.

source_title: Find a repeat in a tune
source_description: Find a phrase that comes back in a tune you can sing or play slowly.

source_title: Mark a rest while you clap
source_description: Clap a short pattern that includes a silence you can point to.

source_title: Name a loud and a soft moment
source_description: In a piece of music or a room, name one louder moment and one softer moment.
Follow a printed repeat on a simple line of music or a rhythm line, and stop where it says.
Use one object as a talking piece and pass it before the next person speaks.

source_title: Write their words on a parking list
source_description: When a topic is parked, write it in the speaker's words.
Repeat the feeling or importance word they used, without adding your own.

source_title: Set a sample before the batch
source_description: Make or show one sample and get a yes before you make the rest.

source_title: Label left and right on a photo
source_description: Label the left and right of a photo from the viewer's side, and say whose left you mean.

source_title: Trace a crack you will not fill
source_description: Trace the path of a crack on a note or a photo, and do not fill it.

source_title: Make a rubbing of a coin
source_description: Make a rubbing of a coin you may use, and say which side you rubbed.

source_title: Tie a luggage label that stays
source_description: Tie a label to a bag so it stays on when you lift the bag.

source_title: Read a contents page to a page
source_description: Use a contents page to find one section, then check you are on the page it named.

source_title: Keep a quote with its page
source_description: Copy a short quote and the page number in the same note.
Write a question in the margin of your own copy, then try to answer it later.

source_title: Arrange tools in the order you use them
source_description: Lay out the tools for a small task in the order you will pick them up.
Cover a part you have finished so the next step does not mark it.
